newsitem.title: UK: Yeltsin health rumours undermine Russia debt price.
newsitem.headline: Yeltsin health rumours undermine Russia debt price.

text.p: Speculation that President Boris Yeltsin's health may be worse than the Kremlin is admitting preyed on Russian debt prices on Tuesday.
However, by mid-morning prices of Vneshekonombank debt were off their initial lows.
"There are rumours that Yeltsin is extremely ill...prices will stay down until things sort themselves out," one U.S. bank trader said.

Vnesh dollar paper RUVNUSLNS=RR was bid quarter of a point lower at 76-3/4 cents in the dollar, around its lowest levels since mid-December, and compared to a record high of around 82 cents a month earlier.
The Kremlin plans its next bulletin on Yeltsin's health after his doctors meet at 1400 gmt on Tuesday.
A spokeswoman said she had no information on when the 65-year-old leader might be released from hospital where he is being treated for pneumonia.
Yeltsin's political opponents are now questioning his ability to rule and suggest he step down.
ING Barings analyst Philip Poole said the most difficult scenario would be for an almost incapacitated Yeltsin to limp through in office, which could destabilise the country.
"The risk is not that there will be a presidential race -- we have to face that at some point anyway -- but more the issue of what happens in the absence of a strong president," he said.
The rest of the market was steady.
Bulgarian Bradys have largely recovered their composure after the ruling Socialists agreed to discuss opposition demands for an early election.
The political crisis has to be sorted out before Bulgaria can expect any external help to stop its rapid economic decline.

Traders said the main opposition party, if in power, might do a better job than the current leaders which they criticised for having done very little in two years of power to prevent economic collapse, warning that default was a real possibility by the middle of this year unless money starts to come in.
